Thanks for the clear asks. I've pulled together a concise operational proposal (attached) that maps notice windows, evidence handoff SLAs, and an escalation matrix for MSA + Order Form situations. Summary of the main points below — full detail in the attached PDF and proposed redline.

- Notice cadence: 10 business days to provide initial written notice after an allegation; 30 calendar days for a complete evidence packet (unless parties agree to extend for good cause).
- Interim response SLA: Redwood acknowledges notice within 48 business hours and assigns a named evidence liaison within 3 business days.
- Evidence transfer: Secure SFTP or shared drive with PII-redaction checklist; standard NDA in place for counsel within 48 hours of request.
- Defense control: Redwood offers to retain defense control for third-party claims but will exclude claims solely arising from Customer-provided training data or explicit customer instructions that cause the output. For AI-generated-output carveouts we propose the customer undertakes indemnity.
- Escalation matrix: contact list in the PDF — Engineer (24h), Legal liaison (48h), VP Legal (72h), Exec escalation (96h) with explicit criteria for escalation (e.g., injunction risk, statutory damages > $500k, regulator notice).

I attached: RDW_Indemnity_Notice_Cadence_v1.pdf (operational playbook) and a redline doc that has suggested Order Form language. If Novex wants a narrower carveout or alternate windows, flag the two items you want us to run up the chain and we'll coordinate with legal and sales leadership.

Karthik / Laura —

Quick legal take (high level):

- Windows: 10 business days initial notice / 30 calendar evidence packet are fine as an operational compromise. I recommend we add a "good faith extension" clause for complex discovery where we commit to update cadence every 15 days if we need more time.
- Acks/SLA: 48 business hours to acknowledge is acceptable; 3 business days to name liaison is borderline but doable if CS agrees.
- Defense control: We should not accept an absolute customer retention of defense control for third-party claims — standard approach is Redwood offers to assume defense control but will not do so for claims that are solely attributable to Customer training data or willful misconduct. For the AI-generated-output carveout: we can accept a narrow carveout limited to (i) output that was solely produced from Customer-supplied proprietary training datasets and (ii) where Customer had a contractual obligation to feed that dataset and the model used those exact prompts (so-called deterministic-output carveout).
- Escrow trigger: reasonable to propose escrow activation thresholds (e.g., > $500k or a filed complaint seeking injunctive relief). We should avoid open-ended escrow obligations.

I attached a short redline with annotated language (RDW_OrderForm_Indemnity_Redline_vNovex.docx). I'll add the "good faith extension" wording and the deterministic carveout language; please review.

Subject: Consolidated operational proposal + limited carveout language (per legal)

Sarah —

Thanks for the quick review window. Per our internal discussion (copied Naomi and Laura), we propose the following operational plan and limited legal compromise for Novex to circulate to procurement:

1) Notice & evidence cadence:
   - Initial written notice: within 10 business days of becoming aware of a claim.
   - Complete evidence packet: within 30 calendar days (good faith extension possible; parties to provide status updates every 15 days).

2) Acknowledgment & liaison:
   - Redwood acknowledges receipt within 48 business hours.
   - Named evidence liaison provided within 3 business days.
   - Engineer triage window: initial technical triage within 24 hours of liaison assignment.

3) Evidence handling:
   - Secure SFTP or vendor-managed encrypted Drive; NDA for counsel to be executed within 48 hours of request.
   - Redwood to provide technical snapshot (model, prompt set, token logs where available) subject to data protection constraints.

4) Defense control & carveout (legal compromise):
   - Redwood will accept defense control for third-party IP claims where Redwood's product is the primary alleged source.
   - Limited carveout accepted: Novex would retain indemnity obligations for claims arising solely from Customer-supplied proprietary training datasets or where the output is demonstrably deterministic from customer-supplied prompts (i.e., reproducible without further Redwood processing). This is narrow by design — general "AI output" carveouts are not acceptable.

5) Escrow & escalation:
   - Escrow activation threshold proposed at $500k in asserted damages or a filed complaint seeking injunctive relief.
   - Escalation matrix with 24/48/72/96 hour contact windows as per the attached PDF.

Next steps: if Novex is comfortable, we will produce an Order Form redline reflecting the bullets above and send a DocuSign for signature for the agreed terms. If Novex wants a call, Naomi (legal) and Laura (CS) are available Monday afternoon.

Would you like us to proceed with the redline or schedule the call?

Regards,
